findings.evidence: Right face turn and head tilt are mixed.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Preoperative clinical photograph of a patient with infantile nystagmus syndrome showing the compensatory abnormal head posture (mixed right face turn and head tilt) that characterizes the null-point head posture of the disease; disease attribution supported by the disease-focused article title and the captioned manifestation. B: Frontal clinical photograph with measured head tilt (15°) demonstrating the compensatory abnormal head posture of infantile nystagmus syndrome in a patient whose article title and in-text description attribute the posture to infantile nystagmus syndrome. C: Overhead clinical photograph documenting the compensatory right face turn (25°) that positions the eyes at the nystagmus null point in infantile nystagmus syndrome; attribution supported by the disease-focused title and the captioned manifestation.
panels.attribution_text: Hayashi et al. Vertical Transposition of the Horizontal Rectus Muscles Combined With the Modified Kestenbaum Procedure for Correcting Abnormal Head Posture Due to Infantile Nystagmus Syndrome.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.72602. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Preoperative head posture. (A) Right face turn and head tilt are mixed. (B) Right head tilt of 15°. (C) Right face turn of 25° (overhead view).
in_text_mentions: On initial examination, visual acuity was 0.15 (0.7 -1.0D = C-1.0D A 10°) in the right eye and 0.04 (0.8 -5.5D = C-2.0D A 15°) in the left eye, and intraocular pressure was 16 mmHg in the right eye and 17 mmHg in the left eye. The eye position was orthotropic, and the Bielschowsky head tilt test was negative. He had right-beating jerk nystagmus in both eyes, 15° right head tilt, and 25° right face turn (Figure 1).

findings.evidence: Right head tilt was reduced to 3°.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Postoperative clinical photo of a patient with infantile nystagmus syndrome showing residual abnormal head posture (right head tilt), a recognized manifestation of the disease. B: Overhead clinical photo of the same patient showing abnormal head posture/face turn after surgery for infantile nystagmus syndrome-related AHP.
panels.attribution_text: Hayashi et al. Vertical Transposition of the Horizontal Rectus Muscles Combined With the Modified Kestenbaum Procedure for Correcting Abnormal Head Posture Due to Infantile Nystagmus Syndrome.. Cureus 2024. doi:10.7759/cureus.72602. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Postoperative head posture. (A) Right head tilt was reduced to 3°. (B) Right face turn was slightly overcorrected, 5° to the left (overhead view).
in_text_mentions: One month postoperatively, the right head tilt was reduced to 3°, and the right face turn was slightly overcorrected (5° to the left), which significantly improved the AHP (Figure 4).
